rationale: Purpose-built framework for benchmarking multi-agent systems directly (built-in single- and multi-agent datasets for comparison), the clearest direct fit found for evaluating networks of interacting AI agents.

Most of its task suite is single-agent-vs-environment, but it includes an Avalon task merged from AvalonBench that is explicitly a multi-agent framework (social deduction requiring multiple interacting agents), giving it genuine (if partial) coverage of RQ24's specific multi-agent-network framing.

Directly implements a dynamic simulation environment (real, not templated, computer environments) purpose-built to better reflect real-world conditions for agent evaluation -- exactly the design problem RQ28 asks about.
Directly unifies evaluation of unlearning technique success across multiple established benchmarks (TOFU/MUSE/WMDP) and 10+ metrics -- exactly what RQ83 asks how to do.

TOFU/MUSE's metric suites include retention/utility metrics alongside forget-quality, i.e. they measure whether unlearning caused unwanted side-effects on untargeted knowledge -- directly relevant to RQ84's side-effect concern.
Directly implements attribution of generated text to specific pretraining/fine-tuning data samples, which is exactly what RQ12 asks whether is achievable.
A cross-domain, taxonomy-classified catalog of real AI incidents is a direct empirical resource for studying how potential risks differ across domains, which is exactly RQ95's question.

Implements exactly the cryptographic method RQ42 asks about: deterministic per-entity HMAC-SHA256 hashing lets user-interaction data be correlated/analyzed across requests without revealing individual identities or storing raw PII.
